subject: english-studies
title: Writing a formal letter
summary: The layout, tone and parts of a formal letter, as expected in BECE and WASSCE.

lesson.text: A formal letter is written to someone in an official position: a principal, a chairman, an editor, a company. It must follow a fixed layout and use polite, serious language.

items: 1. Writer's address, top right, followed by the date.
2. Receiver's title and address, on the left, below the date.
3. Salutation: Dear Sir, Dear Madam, or Dear Sir/Madam.
4. Title (heading) in capitals or underlined, saying what the letter is about.
5. Body: an opening paragraph giving the reason for writing, middle paragraphs with details, and a closing paragraph.
6. Subscript: Yours faithfully, then your signature and full name.
No slang, short forms (don't, can't) or greetings like "How are you?".
Be clear and to the point.

lesson.title: Opening of a letter to a local government chairman
steps: THE POOR STATE OF THE ROAD TO OKE-ADO MARKET
I write on behalf of the traders of Oke-Ado to draw your attention to the bad state of the road leading to our market...

lesson.text: When you start with "Dear Sir" or "Dear Madam", end with "Yours faithfully". If you start with the person's name (Dear Mr Bello), end with "Yours sincerely". Note the small f and s; never "Yours Faithfully".
Examiners mark layout as well as content. Practise the layout until you can write it without thinking.

questions.prompt: Which subscript is correct for a formal letter that begins "Dear Sir"?
questions.explanation: "Dear Sir" goes with "Yours faithfully", with a capital Y and small f. "Your" without the s is wrong.

questions.prompt: Where does the writer's address go in a formal letter?
questions.explanation: The writer's address goes at the top right, with the date under it.

questions.prompt: Which of these does NOT belong in a formal letter?
questions.explanation: Personal greetings belong in informal letters. A formal letter goes straight to its purpose.

questions.prompt: What comes immediately after the salutation?
questions.explanation: After "Dear Sir," comes the title, which tells the reader what the letter is about.

questions.prompt: Which sentence has the right tone for a formal letter?
options: I'm writing coz the road is bad.
Abeg fix this road sharp sharp.
I write to complain about the condition of the road.
questions.explanation: Formal letters use full, polite standard English, with no short forms (I'm, coz) or Pidgin.
